body:
# Summary

`agentdev-codex` mounted all of `~/.codex` as one literal volume shared across every worktree, which has the same bug PR #36 just fixed for Claude: `reinstall-agentdev-codex.sh` deregisters and re-adds the marketplace on every `postStartCommand`, so starting a second worktree clobbered the first one's Codex plugin marketplace registration. This scopes `~/.codex` per worktree the same way `~/.claude` already is, and shares only Codex's `auth.json` — not its plugins, sessions, logs, or sqlite state.

## What Changed

- `agentdev-codex` moves from `docker-compose.yml`'s shared external volumes into `devcontainer.json`'s per-project mounts, matching the existing `agentdev-claude` mount. Compose now scopes it per devcontainer instance instead of sharing one copy across every worktree.
- Codex has no equivalent of Claude's `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` — `CODEX_HOME` is a single directory for all of Codex's state, not just auth — so only `auth.json` can be shared, and only via the same file-in-a-shared-volume-plus-symlink trick already used for `~/.claude.json`. New `.devcontainer/scripts/link-codex-auth.sh` persists `auth.json` in the shared volume and symlinks it into `~/.codex`, called from both `postCreateCommand.sh` and `postStartCommand.sh` (mirroring how `reinstall-agentdev-codex.sh` already runs from both hooks).
- Claude's `agentdev-claude-auth` volume and Codex's new auth volume are consolidated into one shared `agentdev-agents-auth` volume (`/root/.agents-auth`), one subdirectory per agent, instead of a volume per agent.
- Updated `README.md`, `docs/using-as-template.md`, and `docs/repository-structure.md` to describe the new volume layout.

## Why

Every worktree fights over the same Codex marketplace registration and plugin cache today, the same way Claude did before PR #36. Scoping Codex's state per worktree while keeping its login credentials shared avoids re-authenticating Codex on every rebuild, without worktrees clobbering each other's installed plugins.

## How to Test

- `shellcheck` on all touched/new shell scripts, and the repository's local Super-Linter pass (`super-linter-local.sh`, mirrors CI's `Reformat code` job) — both clean.
- Parsed `docker-compose.yml` (YAML) and `devcontainer.json` (JSONC) to confirm the renamed/consolidated `agentdev-agents-auth` volume, the new `agentdev-codex` per-project mount, and the updated `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` path are all present and consistent.
- Ran `link-codex-auth.sh` against the real live `~/.codex/auth.json` in this devcontainer: verified the file moved into the shared volume with a matching checksum, correct `0700`/`0600` permissions, the symlink survived a re-run (idempotent), and `codex login status` still resolved real credentials through the symlink afterward.
- Verified empirically, in a disposable scratch `CODEX_HOME` under `./.tmp` (cleaned up after): `codex login --with-api-key` writes through a symlinked `auth.json` in place (content updates, symlink survives); `codex logout` unlinks the local path outright instead of clearing it in place, which is why `link-codex-auth.sh` has to re-run on every `postStartCommand.sh`, not just `postCreateCommand.sh`.
- Did not rebuild the devcontainer end-to-end (that would disrupt the running session); the currently running container still uses the pre-change mounts and will pick up this config on its next rebuild.

## Breaking Changes

- None to the codebase, but both agents will need to re-authenticate once after this lands: the old `agentdev-claude-auth` and the old whole-tree `agentdev-codex` volumes are abandoned in favor of the new consolidated `agentdev-agents-auth` volume, with no data migration between them.

## Migration

- None required beyond the one-time re-authentication noted above.

## Related

- Builds on #36 and #37, which made the same fix for `~/.claude`.

author: gaberoo322
body:
Closes #3825

Rank the weekly-quota culprit report by **weighted** burn (not raw tokens), with cache-write broken out as its own column, an explicit `interactive` unattributed residual, and a meter-validation section. Cache writes are 57–68% of real subscription burn and were **invisible** in every current ranking, because the `weightedTokens` fold hardcoded 3 of 4 token categories at weight 1.0 and the family weights were unset — so `weightedQuotaBurn` was an identity and every ranking surface ordered consumers by raw cache-read volume (85% of volume, ~25% of cost). The data was already collected correctly (`bySkillByModel` / `byDispatchKind` carry all four categories per family); the defect was the fold.

## What changed

- **`weightedTokens` generalized to four `CategoryWeights`** (`token-math.ts`). The fold now weights all four billed categories — `w.input*input + w.output*output + w.cacheCreation*cacheCreation + w.cacheRead*cacheRead` — instead of hardcoding three at 1.0. Pure + total, no env read.
- **New list-price config namespace** (`config.ts`): `getBurnWeight*` / `getBurnFamily*` readers under `HYDRA_USAGE_BURN_WEIGHT_*` / `HYDRA_USAGE_BURN_FAMILY_*`, defaulting to the list-price ratios (cache read 0.1x / cache write 1.25x 5m-TTL / output 5.0x / input 1.0x; family opus 5 / sonnet 3 / haiku 1 by per-MTok input price). These are **deliberately separate** from the live-fold `HYDRA_USAGE_CACHE_READ_WEIGHT` / `HYDRA_QUOTA_WEIGHT_*` knobs: the live fold stays identity-by-default so this PR is behaviour-neutral on the gate, and the report's calibration never leaks into pacing.
- **General four-category fold** (`snapshot-assembly.ts`): `weightedQuotaBurnByCategory(byModel, category, familyWeights)`. The legacy `weightedQuotaBurn(byModel, wCache, weights)` signature is **unchanged** — it now delegates with `{input:1, output:1, cacheRead:wCache, cacheCreation:1}`, so `/api/usage` + the Class Yield Scoreboard are byte-identical (one weighting definition, CONTEXT.md).
- **`scripts/cost/weighted-quota-report.ts`** — the ranked culprit report. Pure helpers (`rankConsumers`, `sampleTimestamps`, `computeWeightedCurve`, `decideTracking`, `buildReport`, `renderTextReport`, exported + unit-tested) + an I/O `main()` that walks the **since-reset** transcript window (foreign-provider tokens excluded per #3769), ranks both by dispatch-kind and by skill, prints cache-write as its own column, reports the `interactive` unattributed residual, and validates the weighted % against the meter's `percentLast7d`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Ranked report with cache-write visible** — yes; `renderRankTable` emits a `cacheWrite` column per row, populated from each row's `categories.cacheCreation` aggregate.
2. **Shares + residual sum to real burn** — yes; `rankConsumers` uses the FULL total (every consumer, including `interactive`) as the share denominator, so ranked shares + the residual = 100% of measured weighted burn, never a partial slice. The residual is not pinned last — it ranks by its earned burn.
3. **Validation: weighted % tracks meter** — the report normalises the weighted total against `HYDRA_USAGE_WEEKLY_QUOTA_TOKENS` and compares to `percentLast7d`, stating the ratio + a within-`--tolerance` (default 2x, both directions) verdict. **Honest limitation stated in the report:** historical `percentLast7d` is not persisted today (the weekly snapshot stores raw per-skill totals only), so the meter correlation is asserted at the single current point while ≥3 reconstructed weighted samples span the window on the WEIGHTED axis. When the anchor is unset (window degrades to rolling-7d), the quota is unset, or the meter is unreachable, the comparison is **withheld** and the weights are NOT presented as calibrated.
4. **Statement of weights + caveat** — the validation section prints the exact category + family weights used and labels them a **LIST-PRICE PROXY** for an opaque OAuth meter (the dollar fields are null), i.e. a hypothesis validated against the meter, not an assumption.
5. **`weightedTokens` non-identity for default config + per-category regression** — pinned in `test/token-math.test.mts`: an isolation test asserts each of the four categories contributes at its own configured weight, and the default-config fold is shown NOT to equal `.total`.

scope-justification: `test/usage-tracker.test.mts` — criterion 5 requires changing `weightedTokens` to a four-weight `CategoryWeights` signature, and this file's three pre-existing assertions (a "weightedTokens helper" block) called the old `(breakdown, number)` form, which no longer compiles. They were rewritten to the new shape (all-1.0 reduces to `.total`; the list-price config yields a fixed weighted value; a zeroed cacheRead weight isolates the axis). This is the only out-of-scope file touched (1 of 10 changed; well under the scope-check soft-fail threshold of count>3 / ratio>0.8).

## Files in scope

- src/cost/token-math.ts
- src/cost/config.ts
- src/cost/usage-tracker.ts
- src/cost/snapshot-assembly.ts
- src/cost/index.ts
- test/token-math.test.mts
- test/cost-config.test.mts
- scripts/cost/weighted-quota-report.ts
- test/weighted-quota-report.test.mts

## Friction Report

- **Signature cascade into an out-of-scope test file.** Generalizing `weightedTokens` to `CategoryWeights` (criterion 5) necessarily broke the three `weightedTokens` assertions in `test/usage-tracker.test.mts` (out of scope). Rewrote them to the new shape rather than keeping a deprecated 2-arg overload — an overload would have left the identity fold alive and defeated the criterion. Scope-justified above.
- **Criterion 3 cannot be satisfied literally in a single run.** The OAuth meter is read live only (`percentLast7d` is not persisted), so "≥3 sampled points" of *meter* correlation is impossible without a persistence change that is out of scope. Resolved by reconstructing ≥3 WEIGHTED-burn samples spanning the window (`computeWeightedCurve`) + comparing the current weighted % to the current meter %, and stating the limitation explicitly in the report body so the weights are never presented as calibrated beyond what the data supports.
- **`npm test` first run reported 2 fail; the `test:debug` re-run was 0 fail / 7008 tests.** The two were the known worktree-local flakes (the `node:test` suite shares one Redis DB; `--test-concurrency=1` debug run is deterministic). `typecheck` clean; `typecheck:test` ratchet 4/4 with no new rot.

## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
Tier 3 from #128.

## The trap

MLX aborts the process when it cannot load its Metal library. A bare `swift test` therefore dies on the first test that touches MLX — in practice the **second test of the run**:

```
Test Case '-[SwiftBuddyTests.AudioExtractionTests testAudio_Base64WAVExtraction]' passed
Test Case '-[SwiftBuddyTests.AudioExtractionTests testAudio_LongAudioChunking]' started.
MLX error: Failed to load the default metallib. library not found …
```

Everything after that goes unexecuted, and the output still reads as a short, passing run. A contributor can run the tests, see green, and have exercised **one assertion out of ~250**.

CI is unaffected — it installs the metallib inline (`ci.yml`, "Install MLX Metal library"), which is exactly why this went unnoticed.

## The fix

`scripts/install-test-metallib.sh` performs that same step locally. It prefers a metallib already produced by `build.sh`, otherwise pulls one from the `mlx` wheel as CI does, then installs it beside the built products **and inside every `.xctest` bundle** — MLX looks for a metallib colocated with the running binary, which for tests is inside the bundle, not next to it.

```bash
swift build --build-tests
scripts/install-test-metallib.sh
swift test
```

## Measured

| | Executed tests | Failures |
|---|---|---|
| before | **1** | 0 |
| after | **245** | 0 |

README documents the sequence in the Testing section.

## Note

This also means the "full suite green" claims made while fixing #108/#110/#112 were per-suite (`--filter`) runs, not a single invocation — the single invocation was never possible. It is now, and it passes.
